title: Growing an Overnight Bacteria Culture
author: Katy M Monteith
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vbne2me

steps.title: Prepare LB broth volume
steps.instruction: Pour the appropriate volume of LB broth into an autoclaved conical container, ensuring the liquid does not rise above the container’s widest point; for a 10 mL inoculation use a 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Inoculate broth
steps.instruction: Add the frozen bacterial aliquot to the LB broth, or alternatively pick a single colony with an inoculation loop from a plate and swirl the loop in the broth until the cells are visibly floating.

substeps.instruction: Pick isolated colony with loop, suspend in broth

steps.title: Loosely seal container
steps.instruction: Seal the container loosely—secure a tube lid with tape or cover a flask with tinfoil—to allow gas exchange.

steps.title: Incubate with shaking
steps.instruction: Place the tube or flask in an orbital shaker set to ~140 rpm and incubate at the optimal temperature for the strain (typically 30 °C or 37 °C) for 12–14 hours. After incubation, measure the culture’s optical density at 600 nm; use the culture when OD600 is ~0.6–0.8 (exponential phase). If reinoculating into a larger volume, the exact growth phase is less critical, though lag or stationary phase inocula will delay reaching exponential growth.

substeps.instruction: Proceed with use or reinoculation as appropriate
